summary: Codex CLI has no per-call model-request identity, so DelegationSigningProxy dedups Responses on the content fingerprint, which can wrong-merge two distinct same-content calls within one stage/attempt.
probe_method: Behavioral probe. The probe runs the pinned codex binary non-interactively (codex exec) with a dummy credential against a loopback mock OpenAI Responses upstream that records every request, and observes the ACTUAL wire surface Codex sends on /responses: the set of request header names and request body field names. This sees the real protocol, including request-layer headers that a static struct-size check is blind to (a request-level Idempotency-Key header would never change ModelProviderInfo's element count). The probe asserts the observed surface equals this audited baseline; any new or removed name fails the probe and forces a manual audit before KB-001 can be touched. This deliberately replaces the prior struct element-count probe: element-count could not see request-layer additions, was blind to add+delete pairs, and could trip on unrelated struct changes, so its 'exact / zero-false-positive' claim did not hold. Element-count is no longer used.
behavioral_probe_scope: The probe compares sorted SETS of header names and body field names, excluding the per-request transport headers host and content-length. A value-only change (e.g. the version string inside user-agent on a pin bump, or a new session id value) does NOT trip the probe — only a new or removed NAME does. When a name appears, the failure message names it so the auditor can decide whether it carries per-call identity. Per-call VARIATION (an existing field gaining per-call semantics without a name change) is not machine-detectable from a name set; it is covered by the manual audit that every pin bump triggers (the strict CI job re-runs this probe against the new binary). The probe runs only under OPENMONTAGE_CODEX_PROBE_STRICT=1 (dedicated CI job that installs the pinned Codex); generic CI without Codex skips it while the manifest invariants run unconditionally.
unblock_condition: Codex model-provider config or the model request carries a value that varies per call (per-call header interpolation, or a stable per-call Idempotency-Key on the Responses request), confirmed by observing Codex's actual request surface. When the behavioral probe detects a new identity-carrying header/field, run the manual per-call-variation audit; only then remove the content_fingerprint fallback in openmontage/delegation_proxy.py and close KB-001.

external_tracker.next_action: File external_tracker.issue_draft verbatim (or adapted) to openai/codex before Next review; on filing, set status=FILED and filed_issue=<issue URL> in both docs/codex_capability_probe.json and docs/KNOWN_BLOCKERS.md.

issue_draft.title: Per-call model-request identity for Responses (per-call header interpolation, or a stable per-call Idempotency-Key)
issue_draft.body:
## Problem

When a downstream proxy signs and routes Codex OpenAI-compatible traffic, it needs a value that varies per model request to dedup/replay safely. Codex's `/responses` requests currently carry only per-turn/per-session identity (session-id, thread-id) and a per-request x-client-request-id. Within a single stage/attempt, two genuinely distinct but byte-identical same-content `/responses` calls cannot be told apart, so a proxy that dedups to avoid double-billing/invocation collapses the second call onto the first cached response — losing the second call's execution, billing, and attribution.

## Observed request surface (codex-cli 0.146.0, Responses wire_api)

Request header names: accept, authorization, content-type, originator, session-id, thread-id, user-agent, x-client-request-id, x-codex-beta-features, x-codex-turn-metadata, x-codex-window-id. Request body fields: client_metadata, include, input, instructions, model, parallel_tool_calls, prompt_cache_key, reasoning, store, stream, tool_choice, tools. None of these vary per model request in a way a proxy can use as a stable per-call key.

## Request

A value that varies per call on the Responses request — either per-call header interpolation (e.g. a configurable header whose value is set per invocation), or a stable per-call `Idempotency-Key` header on the `/responses` request — so downstream proxies can key replay strictly on per-call identity instead of the request content fingerprint. This would let signed-routing proxies guarantee distinct same-content calls are never wrong-merged.

## Workaround in use

DelegationSigningProxy currently dedups Responses on a content fingerprint when no per-call identity is present (bounded to one stage/attempt; rare in practice). A first-class per-call identity would remove this wrong-merge window entirely.
